newsitem.title: UK: TWO ARGENTINIAN PROVINCES PLAN TAX RECEIPT BONDS.
newsitem.headline: TWO ARGENTINIAN PROVINCES PLAN TAX RECEIPT BONDS.

text.p: Two Argentinian provinces are planning to launch dollar bonds backed by tax receivables, bankers said on Wednesday.
The province of Corrientes is preparing a $112 million five-year bond and the province of Tucuman was planning a similar $200 million transaction, they said.
BankBoston, Banco de Galicia and Banco Rio were tipped as lead managers for the Corrientes deal and Bear Stearns for the Tucuman issue.
Bankers said the Corrientes deal would be an amortising FRN with an average life around three years. Roadshows for the issue are due to be completed this week, they said.
A third Argentine province, Mendoza, is also holding roadshows this week for a dollar bond.
It is expected to issue a $250 million two-tranche deal with five- and 10-year maturities via CSFB and BankBoston. -- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
